title.narrative: PNG Inclusive Green Finance Implementation Roadmap (PNG IGFR)

description.narrative: Scale up access to green finance for sustainable activities and investments that are aligned to PNG’s Green Taxonomy, while mitigating the risk for financial institutions at the same time

Under the IGFP Roadmap, BPNG is developing Green Financial Instruments . The purpose of these instruments is to incentivize and scale up green and inclusive lending in PNG, in line with the national Inclusive and Green Taxonomy. The GFIs will channel resources and de-risk the financial sector to strengthen PNG’s green finance portfolio. The Bank of Papua New Guinea launched the Inclusive Green Finance Policy (IGFP) in 2023. As part of this initiative, the Green Finance Centre (GFC) was established in 2024 as a department under BPNG, with initial funding from the Government of New Zealand and ongoing operational support from the AFD. The IGFP is implemented by the GGGI in partnership with BPNG, the Climate Change and Development Authority and the Department of Treasury . The GFC is tasked with implementing the IGFP Policy and the Green Finance Roadmap, which aim to strengthen Papua New Guinea’s financial ecosystem by: · Embedding green finance principles · Creating an enabling environment for mobilizing climate finance, and · Promoting green investments across the country. The GFC also serves as a national platform for collaboration with financial stakeholders to scale up green financing at both national and sub-national levels. Through AFD’s regional initiative, the Greening the Pacific Financial Systems (GPFS) Program , the GFC is receiving technical and financial support to deliver priority components of PNG’s Inclusive Green Finance Policy Roadmap. Under this program, GFC is leading the rollout of two flagship instruments: Green Refinancing Facility , and Green Guarantee Facility To date, AFD has committed EUR 1.8 million in seed capital for the GRF, with discussions underway for additional funding for the GGF. Beyond financial instruments, AFD’s support also extends to Technical assistance to integrate PNG’s Green Taxonomy into financial sector lending practices, and Development of a Green Catalogue to guide green loan eligibility.
